title: One batch, not the whole queue
dek: A configurable job limit caps each send while leaving the rest of the queue for later drains.

sections.title: Each send took everything waiting
sections.content:
The worker sent jobs to /jobs by draining a pending array. On each call to tick, it passed that array to drain and sent the returned jobs. The drain used pending.splice(0), which removed every entry from the array.

That made the pending queue determine the size of each send. Ten waiting jobs meant a batch of ten; a thousand waiting jobs meant a batch of a thousand. The worker had no configured limit between the queue and the send.

sections.title: A busy queue needed a smaller next step
sections.content:
The missing control was a maximum number of jobs per send. If 250 jobs were waiting, the old drain handed all 250 to the sender. With the new default limit of 100, that same drain returns the first 100 and leaves 150 pending. Later drains can take the remainder in further batches.

The guarantee concerns job count. It does not bound job memory or processing time: a batch of 100 jobs still has no promised byte size or duration. This distinction defines what the new setting controls.

sections.title: Validate the limit, then drain only that many
sections.content:
The change puts a validated limit on the existing drain-and-send path. In config.ts, BATCH_LIMIT supplies the value through the environment. If it is absent, the limit defaults to 100. The configuration module converts the value to a number and checks it at startup.

{{CODE:0}}

The guard rejects anything that does not become a positive integer. A value of zero, a fraction, or nonnumeric text throws the stated error when the module loads. The worker therefore receives a validated setting.

In queue.ts, the drain now accepts that limit as the number of entries to remove.

{{CODE:1}}

The second argument to splice supplies the cap. The function returns the first jobs in array order and leaves every remaining entry in the same pending array. If fewer jobs are waiting than the limit allows, it returns only those available.

In worker.ts, the worker imports batchLimit alongside endpoint from the configuration module. It passes the setting into the drain before sending the result.

{{CODE:2}}

This connects startup validation to each send without changing the destination. The batch comes from the bounded drain; later drains can consume the entries left behind.

Per-tenant scheduling remains out of scope because the queue has no tenant key. The limit operates on the existing array order, with no tenant-based selection.

sections.title: A cap on the next send
sections.content: PR #108 replaces whole-queue drains with batches capped by BATCH_LIMIT, defaulting to 100. Startup validation requires a positive integer. Each worker tick sends only the bounded drain result, leaving the rest queued for later drains. The result is a per-send job-count bound, not a memory or processing-time bound; tenant-aware scheduling remains outside the change because the queue has no tenant key.
